title: Question 1
stem:
A satellite is in a circular orbit of radius r about the Earth of mass M, as illustrated in Fig. 1.1.
The mass of the Earth may be assumed to be concentrated at its centre.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Show that the period T of the orbit of the satellite is given by the expression
$T^{2} =\frac{4\pi ^{2}r 3}{GM}$
where G is the gravitational constant. Explain your working.

markscheme_points.text: gravitational force provides/is the centripetal force
GMm / r 2 = mv 2 / r or GMm / r 2 = mrω2 and v = 2πr / T or ω = 2π / T
or acceleration due to gravity is the centripetal acceleration (B1) GM / r 2 = v 2 / r or GM / r 2 = rω2 and v = 2πr / T or ω = 2π / T (M1) with algebra to T 2 = 4π2r3 / GM

hints: Hint 1: Identify all given parameters and units, then recall the fundamental equation in gravitational fields and orbital mechanics connecting them.
Hint 2: Rearrange the algebraic equation to isolate the target variable before substituting numerical values.
Hint 3: Ensure all quantities are expressed in standard SI base units and verify your intermediate arithmetic before writing the final result to 2 or 3 significant figures.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.text:
A satellite in geostationary orbit appears to remain above the same point on the Earth
and has a period of 24 hours.
State two other features of a geostationary orbit.
hints: Hint 1: Focus on the physical mechanism in gravitational fields and orbital mechanics that causes this behavior.
Hint 2: Rearrange the algebraic equation to isolate the target variable before substituting numerical values.
parts.proper_answer: equatorial orbit/orbits (directly) above the equator; from west to east

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text:
The mass M of the Earth is $6.0 \times 10^{24}\,\mathrm{kg}$.
Use the expression in (a) to determine the radius of a geostationary orbit.
$radius = m $
hints: Hint 1: Identify all given parameters and units, then recall the fundamental equation in gravitational fields and orbital mechanics connecting them.
Hint 2: Rearrange the algebraic equation to isolate the target variable before substituting numerical values.
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Identify Governing Principle**
State the core physical principle governing this problem: Gravitational fields and orbital mechanics. Identify the relationship between the given quantities.

Step 2: **Substitute Values & Calculate**
Work through the substitution and calculation systematically:
(24 × 3600)2 = 4π2r 3 / (6.67 × 10-11 × 6.0 × 1024); r 3 = 7.57 × 1022 r = 4.2 × 107 m
Verify intermediate arithmetic carefully.

Step 3: **Units & Significant Figures**
State the final result clearly with appropriate significant figures (typically 2 or 3 s.f.) and standard SI units.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
A global positioning system (GPS) satellite orbits the Earth at a height of $2.0 \times 10^{4}$ km above
the Earth’s surface.
The radius of the Earth is $6.4 \times 10^{3}$ km.
Use your answer in (b)(ii) and the expression
T ^{2} ∝ $r^{3}$
to calculate, in hours, the period of the orbit of this satellite.
$period = hours $
hints: Hint 1: Identify all given parameters and units, then recall the fundamental equation in gravitational fields and orbital mechanics connecting them.
Hint 2: Rearrange the algebraic equation to isolate the target variable before substituting numerical values.
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Identify Governing Principle**
State the core physical principle governing this problem: Gravitational fields and orbital mechanics. Identify the relationship between the given quantities.

Step 2: **Substitute Values & Calculate**
Work through the substitution and calculation systematically:
(T / 24)2 = {(2.64 × 107) / (4.23 × 107)}3; = 0.243 T = 12 hours; or k (= T 2 / r 3) = 242 / (4.23 × 107)3 (B1) k = 7.61 × 10-21 T 2 (= kr 3) = 7.61 × 10-21 × (2.64 × 107)3 = 140 T = 12 hours
Verify intermediate arithmetic carefully.

Step 3: **Units & Significant Figures**
State the final result clearly with appropriate significant figures (typically 2 or 3 s.f.) and standard SI units.
